clue.text: Composer, from the start in intricate style

indicators.note: the composer's name is drawn out from within the run of letters that follows

explanation.surface: A remark that some composer works in an intricate style from the very outset.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs through 'sTART IN Intricate'; 'from' signals that it is taken out of those words, and 'the' and 'style' only dress the surface. Giuseppe Tartini was an Italian violinist and composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartini was an eighteenth-century Italian violinist who wrote the Devil's Trill sonata, so he is a composer.

clue.text: The male ferret attacked small humanoid

parts.note: taken as written
a hob is the name for a male ferret

explanation.surface: A male ferret has gone for a little creature.
explanation.walkthrough: A hob is a male ferret (a jill is the female). Tolkien's title character is the small humanoid of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's hobbit is a small human-like creature, and his book of that title names one.

clue.text: Rioters out of control, like Ralph, swagger

explanation.surface: Unruly rioters strut about like some swaggering lad called Ralph.
explanation.walkthrough: Ralph Roister Doister is the blustering hero of the earliest English comedy (Nicholas Udall, c.1552), so 'like Ralph' points to the verb his name puns on.
explanation.definitionFit: To roister is to bluster and revel noisily, the swaggering manner of Udall's Ralph Roister Doister.

clue.text: Her sister mourned becomingly

explanation.surface: A woman's sister grieved in a seemly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mourned becomingly' turns round the title Mourning Becomes Electra, so 'Her' is Electra; her sister was sacrificed by Agamemnon at Aulis.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Agamemnon's daughters include Electra and the girl sacrificed at Aulis, making them sisters.

clue.text: "What witchcraft now have these — of the Devil been a hatching here?" (Farquhar)

explanation.walkthrough: Fill the gap: the phrase is 'these imps of the Devil', little demons who do the Devil's work.
explanation.definitionFit: Little demons serving Satan are his minor fiends, which fits 'of the Devil' in the quotation.

clue.text: Report of speaking vocalist may add to value of first edition

explanation.walkthrough: 'Report of' signals the sound of the word for a rap artist; the dust jacket of a first edition is called its wrapper, and an intact one raises the price greatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Book collectors call the dust jacket the wrapper, and a first edition with it intact is worth much more.

clue.text: Lawbreaker at party is outspoken novelist

clue.text: Allow first "absurd " dramas made Ionesco tedious

clue.text: Frothy coffees not about to be suggested for opera composer

clue.text: Object of quest by Symons

explanation.definitionFit: Symons's biography The Quest for Corvo hunts down the life of Frederick, the pseudonymous Baron Corvo.

clue.text: Cut out initial hesitation for Miss Wharton

clue.text: I call poem terribly controversial

clue.text: Spanish philosopher also gets say in another form

clue.text: Frank said to be his hero

clue.text: Foothold established by 5 Down in 1957

clue.text: Calvino's was unrestrained

clue.text: Crabbed country existence

explanation.definitionFit: Existence in the countryside, the bleak subject of Crabbe's poems The Village and The Borough.

clue.text: Voltaire epic, with part for a maid

explanation.definitionFit: La Pucelle d'Orléans is Voltaire's comic poem on Joan of Arc, and Joan la Pucelle is her part in Henry VI, Part 1.

clue.text: "All things abided — as they were in their proper places' (Thomas Traherne)
